name: Fay Fuller
blurb: Fuller reached Mount Rainier's Columbia Crest with four men of a Seattle party led by the Rev. Ernest C. Smith; Fay Peak, near Mowich Lake, is named for her.
facts: date: August 10, 1890 | type: first female ascent | region: Mount Rainier NP, WA
prompt: In 1890, a 20-year-old schoolteacher in a flannel bloomer suit, then thought immodest, became the first woman known to reach this summit, and spent the night in a steam-vent ice cave near the top.

name: Phyllis Munday
blurb: Munday topped Mount Robson from the Alpine Club of Canada's 1924 camp; a year later she and her husband Don spied the 'Mystery Mountain' now called Mount Waddington.
facts: date: 1924 | type: first female ascent | region: Mount Robson PP, BC
prompt: In 1924, Vancouver climber Phyllis Munday became the first woman to stand atop the highest peak in the Canadian Rockies. Her guide, Conrad Kain, had led its first ascent 11 years earlier.

name: Henrietta Tuzo
blurb: Mount Tuzo (3,246 m) rises on the Alberta–BC divide in the Valley of the Ten Peaks above Moraine Lake; Tuzo's son was the plate-tectonics pioneer J. Tuzo Wilson.
facts: date: 1906 | type: first ascent | region: Banff NP, AB
prompt: In 1906, Henrietta Tuzo and guide Christian Kaufmann made the first ascent of 'Peak Seven' in a famous row of ten summits above a turquoise lake. The mountain now bears her name.

name: Maëlle Ricker
blurb: Cypress Mountain hosted the 2010 Games' freestyle skiing and snowboarding events, minutes from where Ricker grew up; one of its runs now carries her name.
facts: date: February 16, 2010 | type: Olympic gold | region: North Shore, BC
prompt: On February 16, 2010, a North Vancouver snowboarder won Olympic snowboard cross on this mountain, becoming the first Canadian woman ever to win Olympic gold on home soil.

name: Lindsey Vonn
blurb: The course dropped 770 m down Whistler Mountain's Creekside flank, from Wild Card to Lower Franz's Run; teammate Julia Mancuso took silver.
facts: date: February 17, 2010 | type: Olympic gold | region: Sea-to-Sky, BC
prompt: On February 17, 2010, Lindsey Vonn won the Olympic women's downhill on this mountain, the first US gold ever in the event, on a course where several racers crashed.

name: Alissa St Laurent
blurb: The Canadian Death Race starts and finishes in Grande Cache, Alberta; St Laurent won in 13 h 53 min, under three weeks after a record-setting win at the Sinister 7.
facts: date: August 1, 2015 | type: ultramarathon | region: Grande Cache, AB
prompt: In 2015, an Edmonton runner became the first woman to win this mountain town's 125 km ultramarathon outright, crossing three summits and finishing nearly 90 minutes ahead of the fastest man.

name: Rainier Infinity Loop
blurb: Conceived by the late Chad Kellogg, the loop crosses Mount Rainier's summit twice; its Wonderland Trail legs add up to one full lap of the mountain.
facts: date: July 25–30, 2019 | type: mountain ultramarathon | region: Mount Rainier NP, WA
prompt: In July 2019, Kaytlyn Gerbin and Alex Borsuk became the first all-women team to finish this volcano's 'Infinity Loop': two summits plus a full lap around it on foot, 130+ miles in just over four days.
